AC-5's 'separate process' claim is verified by reading bytes in-process rather than spawning a distinct process; the disk read still substantively checks durability and trailing newline

append reads tail hash then writes without a lock: two concurrent writers both read the same prev_hash and emit forked lines with identical prev_hash, breaking chain integrity (TOCTOU race); no lock in __init__

findings: [low] ledgerlock/ledger.py:27 — `append` has a read-modify-write TOCTOU race: `_tail_hash()` (line 43) reads the tail hash from disk, then `_append_line()` (line 53) appends without holding any lock, so two concurrent `Ledger` writers on the same path can both read the same `prev_hash` and emit two lines with identical `prev_hash`, forking the chain and breaking the tamper-evidence guarantee; no lock exists in `__init__` (line 18). Consequence is chain-integrity corruption, not data disclosure, so low.
